A Counterexample to the Gaussian Completely Monotone Conjecture

Yuzhou Gu ††thanks: sevenkplus.g@gmail.com    Mark Sellke ††thanks: msellke@fas.harvard.edu
Abstract

We provide an explicit probability measure on ℝ\mathbb{R} for which the fifth time derivative of the entropy along the heat flow is positive at some time. This disproves the Gaussian completely monotone (GCM) conjecture (Cheng–Geng ’15) and therefore also the Gaussian optimality conjecture (McKean ’66) and the entropy power conjecture (Toscani ’15). Our proof also implies the existence of a log-concave probability measure on ℝ\mathbb{R} for which the GCM conjecture fails at some order. The explicit counterexample was found by GPT-5.5 Pro.

1 Introduction

Let Pt=et∂x2P_{t}=e^{t\partial_{x}^{2}} denote the heat semigroup on ℝ\mathbb{R}. For a real variable XX with law μ\mu, Pt​μP_{t}\mu is the law of X+2​t​GX+\sqrt{2t}G, where GG is a standard Gaussian independent of XX. For t>0t>0, this measure is represented by the smooth function

pt∗μ,pt(x)=(4πt)−1/2e−x24​t.p_{t}*\mu,\qquad p_{t}(x)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-\frac{x^{2}}{4t}}.

We write

Hμ​(t)=ℋ⁡(Pt​μ)=∫ℝ(pt∗μ)​(x)​log⁡(pt∗μ)​(x)​𝑑x.H_{\mu}(t)=\mathcal{H}(P_{t}\mu)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}(p_{t}*\mu)(x)\log(p_{t}*\mu)(x)\,\,dx.

The Gaussian completely monotone (GCM) conjecture [CG15] states that

(−1)m​Hμ(m)​(t)≥0,m≥1,t>0.(-1)^{m}H_{\mu}^{(m)}(t)\geq 0,\qquad m\geq 1,t>0. (1)

A strengthening of this conjecture is the Gaussian optimality conjecture due to [McK66, Section 12], which states that the left-hand side of (1) is exactly minimized by Gaussian measures when μ\mu has fixed variance. A further strengthening is the entropy power conjecture [Tos15], which asserts that

(−1)m−1​dmd​tm​Nμ​(t)≥0,Nμ​(t)=e−2​Hμ​(t).(-1)^{m-1}\frac{d^{m}}{dt^{m}}N_{\mu}(t)\geq 0,\qquad N_{\mu}(t)=e^{-2H_{\mu}(t)}.

The same conjectures extend to higher dimension d>1d>1 (with an additional factor of 1/d1/d in the exponent of the last expression). It is easy to see that McKean’s conjecture is stronger than GCM, while [Wan24] showed that the entropy power conjecture implies McKean’s conjecture.

In dimension 11, the GCM conjecture has been proved for derivatives of order m≤4m\leq 4 [CG15]. The higher-dimensional version is true up to order m≤2m\leq 2 via Costa’s entropy power inequality [Cos85, Vil00], and in dimension d≤4d\leq 4 for m≤3m\leq 3 [GYG22]. The special case of log-concave probability measures has also attracted considerable interest [Tos15, ZAG18, GYG22, Wan25]. We refer the reader to [Led24, Wan25] and references therein for further discussion of the history of these conjectures.

Our main result is that in dimension 11, the GCM conjecture fails at the fifth order, which is optimal by the result of [CG15] mentioned above. Thus all three related conjectures are false.

Theorem 1.

There exists a probability measure μ\mu on ℝ\mathbb{R} and a time t0>0t_{0}>0 such that

Hμ(5)​(t0)>0.H_{\mu}^{(5)}(t_{0})>0.

For log-concave probability measures, we show that the GCM conjecture also fails.

Theorem 2.

There exists a log-concave probability measure μ\mu on ℝ\mathbb{R}, a time t0>0t_{0}>0, and an integer m≥1m\geq 1, such that

(−1)m​Hμ(m)​(t0)<0.(-1)^{m}H_{\mu}^{(m)}(t_{0})<0.

An explicit order is not obtained, but it must be at least 66, because the GCM conjecture is known to hold for log-concave probability measures up to the fifth order [ZAG18, Wan25].

3 Proof of Theorem 2

We now show that the preceding counterexample leads to a log-concave counterexample, at a higher order. The additional ingredient is backward propagation of complete monotonicity for analytic functions.

Lemma 1 (Backward propagation of complete monotonicity).

Let A>0A>0, and let FF be real analytic on (−A,∞)(-A,\infty). Suppose that

(−1)m​F(m)​(s)≥0,m≥1,s>0.(-1)^{m}F^{(m)}(s)\geq 0,\qquad m\geq 1,\ s>0.

Then the same inequalities hold for all m≥1m\geq 1 and all s∈(−A,∞)s\in(-A,\infty).

Proof.

This is a standard consequence of the local Taylor-series characterization of completely monotone functions; see, e.g., [Wid41, SSV12]. For completeness, we recall the short argument. Set U=−F′U=-F^{\prime}. Then UU is completely monotone on (0,∞)(0,\infty), and all inequalities (−1)n​U(n)≥0(-1)^{n}U^{(n)}\geq 0 extend to 00 by continuity. If they hold at a point cc, then the Taylor expansion at cc gives, for h≥0h\geq 0 sufficiently small,

(−1)n​U(n)​(c−h)=∑j=0∞(−1)n+j​U(n+j)​(c)j!​hj≥0.(-1)^{n}U^{(n)}(c-h)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+j}U^{(n+j)}(c)}{j!}h^{j}\geq 0.

Thus the inequalities propagate locally to the left; a standard connectedness argument propagates them throughout (−A,0](-A,0]. ∎

Proof of Theorem 2.

Let μ\mu be the finitely supported probability measure in (2). We use two elementary facts. First, if a probability measure is supported in [−R,R][-R,R], then its heat evolution is strictly log-concave for every t>R2/2t>R^{2}/2. Indeed, writing πx\pi_{x} for the posterior law of the initial atom conditioned on the endpoint xx, one has

∂x2log⁡(pt∗μ)​(x)=−12​t+Varπx⁡(a)4​t2≤−12​t+R24​t2<0.\partial_{x}^{2}\log(p_{t}*\mu)(x)=-\frac{1}{2t}+\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_{x}}(a)}{4t^{2}}\leq-\frac{1}{2t}+\frac{R^{2}}{4t^{2}}<0.

Second, for a finitely supported initial measure, Hμ​(t)H_{\mu}(t) is real analytic on (0,∞)(0,\infty). Indeed, locally uniformly for tt in a compact subinterval of (0,∞)(0,\infty), the finite Gaussian mixture gtg_{t} and all its tt-derivatives are bounded by a polynomial in |x||x| times e−c​x2e^{-cx^{2}}. Moreover gt​(x)g_{t}(x) has matching Gaussian lower bounds coming from the extreme atoms, so |log⁡gt​(x)|≤C⁡(1+x2)|\log g_{t}(x)|\leq C(1+x^{2}). Thus the Taylor expansion in tt may be integrated termwise by Gaussian domination.

Take TT large enough so that ν=PT​μ\nu=P_{T}\mu is a log-concave probability measure. Suppose, for contradiction, that the GCM conjecture holds for ν\nu. Then

(−1)m​dmd​sm​ℋ​(Ps​ν)≥0,m≥1,s>0.(-1)^{m}\frac{d^{m}}{ds^{m}}\mathcal{H}(P_{s}\nu)\geq 0,\qquad m\geq 1,\qquad s>0.

But Ps​ν=PT+s​μP_{s}\nu=P_{T+s}\mu. Thus the function

F⁡(s)=Hμ​(T+s)F(s)=H_{\mu}(T+s)

is real analytic on (−T,∞)(-T,\infty) and satisfies

(−1)m​F(m)​(s)≥0,m≥1,s>0.(-1)^{m}F^{(m)}(s)\geq 0,\qquad m\geq 1,\ s>0.

By Lemma 1, the same inequalities hold for all m≥1m\geq 1 and all s>−Ts>-T. Taking s=1/3−Ts=1/3-T and m=5m=5 gives

0≤(−1)5​F(5)​(1/3−T)=−Hμ(5)​(1/3),0\leq(-1)^{5}F^{(5)}(1/3-T)=-H_{\mu}^{(5)}(1/3),

which contradicts Proposition 1. ∎

Appendix A Verification code

The following SageMath script gives the rigorous verification used in Proposition 1. The input atoms and weights are exact rationals. All integrations are carried out with Arb ball arithmetic [Joh17] through SageMath’s ComplexBallField.integral; the printed balls are rigorous enclosures.

⬇
1 from sage.all import ComplexBallField, RealBallField, QQ, binomial
2
3 # Increasing PREC tightens the final balls but does not change the input data.
4 PREC = 256
5 C = ComplexBallField(PREC)
6 R = RealBallField(PREC)
7
8 tau = QQ(1) / QQ(3)
9 tau_C = C(tau)
10 normalization = 1 / (4 * C.pi() * tau_C).sqrt()
11
12 # Exact rational atoms and weights for
13 # 0.002 delta_0 + sum_j c_j (delta_{1.8+j} + delta_{-(1.8+j)}).
14 data = [(QQ(0), QQ(2) / QQ(1000))]
15 c = [34, 93, 134, 123, 75, 31, 8, 1]
16 for j, cj in enumerate(c):
17 a = QQ(18) / QQ(10) + QQ(j)
18 w = QQ(cj) / QQ(1000)
19 data.append((-a, w))
20 data.append(( a, w))
21 data.sort(key=lambda z: z[0])
22
23 assert sum(w for _, w in data) == 1
24
25
26 def hermite_phys(n, z):
27 """Physicists’ Hermite polynomial H_n(z), evaluated by recursion."""
28 parent = z.parent()
29 if n == 0:
30 return parent(1)
31 H0 = parent(1)
32 H1 = 2 * z
33 if n == 1:
34 return H1
35 for k in range(1, n):
36 H0, H1 = H1, 2 * z * H1 - 2 * k * H0
37 return H1
38
39
40 def G(z, analytic):
41 """Ball enclosure for d^5/dt^5 (g_t log g_t) at t = 1/3."""
42 rhos = []
43 for a, w in data:
44 y = z - C(a)
45 rho = C(w) * normalization * (-(y * y) / (4 * tau_C)).exp()
46 rhos.append(rho)
47
48 g = sum(rhos, C(0))
49 posterior = [rho / g for rho in rhos]
50
51 K = [C(0)] * 6
52 K[0] = C(1)
53 sqrt_tau = tau_C.sqrt()
54 for n in range(1, 6):
55 s = C(0)
56 for (a, _), pi_i in zip(data, posterior):
57 y = z - C(a)
58 u = y / (2 * sqrt_tau)
59 s += pi_i * hermite_phys(2 * n, u) / ((4 * tau_C) ** n)
60 K[n] = s
61
62 L = [C(0)] * 6
63 # Passing Arb’s analytic flag makes log reject invalid branch enclosures.
64 L[0] = g.log(analytic=analytic)
65 for n in range(1, 6):
66 s = K[n]
67 for r in range(1, n):
68 s -= binomial(n - 1, r - 1) * L[r] * K[n - r]
69 L[n] = s
70
71 q = C(0)
72 for r in range(0, 6):
73 q += binomial(5, r) * K[r] * L[5 - r]
74 return g * q
75
76
77 def integrate_real(a, b):
78 """Rigorous real ball for integral_a^b G(x) dx."""
79 I = C.integral(
80 G,
81 C(a),
82 C(b),
83 abs_tol=R("1e-30"),
84 rel_tol=R("1e-30"),
85 use_heap=True,
86 )
87 # The exact integral is real. This assertion catches failed analytic
88 # continuation or insufficient subdivision.
89 assert I.imag().contains_zero()
90 assert I.imag().above_abs() < R("1e-25")
91 return I.real()
92

95 blocks = [
96 (QQ(0), QQ(1) / 2, "161.9975"),
97 (QQ(1) / 2, QQ(1), "-219.0117"),
98 (QQ(1), QQ(3) / 2, "73.0107"),
99 (QQ(3) / 2, QQ(2), "1.8755"),
100 (QQ(2), QQ(5) / 2, "-49.7406"),
101 (QQ(5) / 2, QQ(3), "78.9371"),

120 finite_total = R(0)
121 for a, b, midpoint in blocks:
122 block = 2 * integrate_real(a, b)
123 finite_total += block
124 displayed = R(midpoint)
125 assert (block - displayed).above_abs() < R("1e-4")
126 print(f"2 * integral_[{a}, {b}] G = {block}")

128 # Tail estimate from the proof:
129 # |2 int_25^infty G(x) dx| <= 2 * 10^8 * exp(-128) / 16.
130 tail_bound = 2 * R("1e8") * (-R(128)).exp() / R(16)
131 assert tail_bound.upper() < R("1e-20").lower()
132
133 lower = finite_total.lower() - tail_bound.upper()
134 upper = finite_total.upper() + tail_bound.upper()
135

137 print("tail bound =", tail_bound)
138 print("certified H^(5)(1/3) interval = [", lower, ",", upper, "]")
